subject: Private Upgrades: audit log requirements (enterprise stakeholders) — event fields + retention
body:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Private Upgrades: audit log requirements (enterprise stakeholders) — event fields + retention
Attachments: redwood-private-upgrades-audit-events-v0.3.xlsx

Team,

Looping you in on auditability requirements coming in from Cascade Financial (regulated VPC private). They’re explicitly tying upgrade/rollback audit logs to their change-management controls.

What they’re asking for (summary):
- Upgrade/rollback audit logs must be tamper-evident (immutability expectation). For Private they’ll accept “immutable in customer-controlled SIEM” as long as Redwood components can reliably forward/export.
- Retention expectation: 13 months minimum for audit events (their policy is 400 days). They want confirmation on default retention and whether it’s configurable.
- Event detail level: they want more than “upgrade started/stopped.” They want step-level outcomes for prechecks, backups, migrations, and rollback invocation.
- Correlation: must correlate to change tickets + an operator identity (SSO) and the target environment/cluster.

I attached our current proposed event list + fields (v0.3). Can you review and confirm what we can commit to for GA vs what is “best effort” / roadmap?

Open questions I need answers on by EOW for the customer:
1) Can we support 400-day retention in the Private control plane audit store? If not, what’s our supported export story + how quickly after event creation do we deliver?
2) Which identity fields are available in Private upgrades (SSO user id vs service account)?
3) Can we guarantee we emit the same event schema across VPC + on-prem (air-gapped) with a stable versioned schema?

Thanks,
Irene

—
Irene Choi
Infrastructure Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Alicia Morgan <alicia.morgan@cascadefg.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Private Upgrades: audit log requirements (enterprise stakeholders) — event fields + retention
Attachments: cascade-audit-log-requirements-followup.pdf

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for pulling this together.

Two clarifications from our side:
1) We need audit logs for upgrade lifecycle events retained for 400 days. If Redwood doesn’t retain that long, we need a supported mechanism to forward the logs to Splunk (HEC) and/or syslog in near-real time.
2) For each upgrade attempt, our auditors typically ask for:
   - who initiated it (SSO identity)
   - what was changed (from version/to version, artifacts)
   - when it happened
   - whether the backup completed successfully before changes were applied
   - whether rollback was invoked, and why

We can be flexible on the transport (Splunk HEC vs syslog), but we can’t accept “logs only visible in UI for 30/90 days.”

Regards,
Alicia Morgan
Director, Security & Risk
Cascade Financial Group


From: Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 10:41 AM
Subject: Re: Private Upgrades: audit log requirements (enterprise stakeholders) — event fields + retention

Irene — makes sense and matches what we’ve been hearing.

Security/compliance POV:
- Retention: For Private, we should not position the Redwood control plane as the system-of-record for 400-day retention unless we’re 100% confident in sizing + backup/restore of the audit store. I recommend:
  (a) default retention (e.g., 30/90 days) in-product for operator convenience, AND
  (b) a supported export/forwarding mechanism to customer SIEM with guidance that customer SIEM satisfies 400-day requirement.
- Immutability: We can say Redwood emits append-only audit events and supports export; tamper-evidence is achieved by forwarding to an immutable destination under customer control (Splunk index with WORM policy, etc.).
- Schema: Strong preference for a versioned schema and explicit event_version field.

Field-level requirements (minimum set):
- event_id (UUID)
- event_type (enum)
- event_version
- occurred_at (RFC3339)
- environment_id / cluster_id
- upgrade_id (stable across an attempt)
- initiated_by (subject id) + initiated_by_type (oidc_user | service_account)
- request_source (cli | ui | api) and client_ip (if available)
- target_version + source_version
- result (success | failure) and error_code / error_summary

Nice-to-have (but probably required for regulated accounts):
- artifact_digests (sha256 for bundle/chart/images)
- backup_id + backup_result + backup_location_ref (not actual secrets)
- rollback_reason + rollback_target_version

I’ll defer to Allison/Connor on where/how we emit/retain today.

Kevin

—
Kevin Osei
GRC / Audit & SIEM Integrations
Redwood Inference


From: Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 12:09 PM
Subject: Re: Private Upgrades: audit log requirements (enterprise stakeholders) — event fields + retention

Adding observability specifics + what’s realistic for GA.

Where events should be emitted:
1) Control plane API: authoritative events for “upgrade attempt created,” “precheck summary,” “backup completed,” “rollout started/completed,” “rollback invoked/completed.”
2) Installer (on-prem and VPC operator CLI): should emit locally too (stdout + local file) and optionally forward to the control plane when connected.

Export story (recommendation):
- Provide an “audit sink” configuration for Private:
  - sink_type: splunk_hec | syslog_tls | otlp_http (if we want future-proof)
  - endpoint, tls config, auth token ref (in secret), batching + retry
- Sinks run inside the customer’s environment, so this works for VPC and for on-prem (including air-gapped if they have internal Splunk/syslog). For fully disconnected on-prem, we at least have deterministic local file logs that can be rotated + handed to auditors.

Retention:
- I agree with Kevin: don’t promise 400 days in Redwood storage. We can specify:
  - Default in-product retention: 30 days (subject to change)
  - Optional extended retention add-on for hosted offerings — but for Private, make it clear the customer SIEM is the long-term store.

Event granularity:
- Cascade is going to want step-level outcomes. That implies we need events for:
  - precheck.<check_name>.pass/fail (or a single event with an array, but arrays complicate schema; better emit per-check w/ correlation_id)
  - backup.start/complete
  - migration.start/complete (duration_ms)
  - helm_phase.control_plane.start/complete and helm_phase.data_plane.start/complete

Note: Your attached spreadsheet (v0.3) includes “steps” as a list. That’s clean conceptually, but it’s a nested payload and some SIEMs are annoying with parsing. If we keep both (structured JSON + flattened key fields) we’ll reduce pain.

Allison

—
Allison Grant
Observability & Audit Signals
Redwood Inference


From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 2:22 PM
Subject: Re: Private Upgrades: audit log requirements (enterprise stakeholders) — event fields + retention

+1 to sink-based export.

Release Eng constraints / commitments I’m comfortable with for GA:
- Stable event schema with event_version and a published schema doc (even if minimal) and changelog. No breaking changes without version bump.
- Correlation IDs:
  - upgrade_id: generated at plan execution start
  - plan_id: deterministic hash of the plan artifact (so support can tie back to exact steps)
  - release_id: Redwood Private release train identifier (maps installer + charts + control plane build)
- Artifact integrity:
  - We can include sha256 digests for the upgrade bundle (on-prem) and chart/image digests where available. (On VPC, image digests are easiest; on-prem bundles: digest is mandatory.)
- Retention statement:
  - “Control plane retains audit events for operational troubleshooting (30 days default). Customers must configure an export sink for long-term retention.”

If Cascade pushes back on 30 days: we can consider making it configurable up to N days based on disk sizing, but I’d rather not commit before we measure impact.

Connor

—
Connor O'Brien
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference


From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Morgan <alicia.morgan@cascadefg.com>
Cc: Dinesh Patel <dinesh.patel@cascadefg.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 5:28 PM
Subject: Re: Private Upgrades: audit log requirements (enterprise stakeholders) — event fields + retention

Alicia — thanks, this is helpful and aligned with what we can support.

Proposed approach for Cascade (what we can commit to):
- Redwood Private will emit upgrade/rollback audit events with a versioned schema (event_version) and stable correlation identifiers (upgrade_id, plan_id).
- Events will include (at minimum): actor identity (OIDC subject when initiated via SSO; service account id when automated), timestamps, source_version/target_version, outcome, and step-level events for prechecks/backup/migrations/rollout/rollback.
- We will support exporting/forwarding audit events to a customer SIEM (e.g., Splunk HEC or syslog over TLS) for your 400-day retention and immutability controls.
- The Redwood control plane retains events for operator troubleshooting for a default period (targeting 30 days) — long-term retention is satisfied via SIEM export.

Two items I want to confirm with you:
1) Is Splunk HEC the preferred integration for your environment, or would syslog/TLS be easier?
2) Do you need artifact integrity fields (e.g., sha256 digest of upgrade bundle / images), or is version + release_id sufficient?

We’ll incorporate this into our Private upgrade GA checklist and can share a draft schema/changelog once it’s finalized.

Best,
Irene

—
Irene Choi
Infrastructure Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference
